correctness.rationale: The midpoint-coordinate cone partition is a disjoint decomposition up to boundaries, with exact outside-simplex integration. The truncated-power identity and inclusion-exclusion box moment formula are valid including dimension-one and empty-inside limiting cases. Summing all sign patterns cancels all outer term knots, leaving an exact degree-at-most-d polynomial. The support endpoint follows from the L1 triangle inequality and continuity, and the one-sided endpoint slope for positive directions from the box-density slab. Standalone exact-rational and independent convex-hull calculations returned CROSSPOLYTOPE_RADIAL_POLYNOMIAL_OK 216; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The available exact and approximation primary sources concern general semi-algebraic volume algorithms and hardness/approximation of two cross-polytope intersections, not an all-ray single-polynomial formula for congruent L1 balls. Relevant indexed work treats cubes, a cube-cross-polytope intersection, or discrete error balls; those statements do not imply the cancellation theorem. The conclusion is provisionally original, not a guarantee of historical priority.
residual_risks: Classical box-spline or multivariate truncated-power theorems could implicitly entail the polynomial collapse without matching words; a direct encompassing theorem was not established or ruled out.
The Bianchi full proof and the 2014 octahedron correlation full derivation were not materially read in their entirety; narrower already-known special cases may exist.
A bounded semantic-index and literature search does not establish definitive historical priority.

value.rationale: Determines complete exact translation-overlap on every ray of a basic centrally symmetric polytope in all dimensions; the absence of internal polynomial knots is a nontrivial structural cancellation, despite general intersections of L1 balls being computationally difficult. The result supplies an exact all-parameter formula and a sharp support asymptotic, useful for covariogram/tomography and overlap-volume calculations without claiming general #P-hard cases are solved.
